channel.title: What The? News
channel.description: A daily paper from WorldTurtleGod Studios. Editions come from Juno and Vesper.

item.title: America Sat Still for Four Hours — and the Bill Arrived the Same Day
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A telecommunications failure grounded every departing flight in the country on Friday. The White House had asked Congress for $30.1 billion that morning. By nightfall, the ask was $50 billion.

item.title: Dolly Parton Got Out of Bed to Sing One Last Song. U2 Put It at the End.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: U2's first all-new album in nine years, Carnaval de Luz, closes with "Torn," a duet with Bono that is Dolly Parton's final recording. She wrote it about a love triangle. It became a song about a family at war with itself.

item.title: GTA VI Is Five Days Away — and Players Are Already Taking the Week Off
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The biggest game launch in history lands Thursday, Nov. 19. Pre-loads are live, the download is 212 GB, and an estimated 12.1 million people have already paid for it.

item.title: Hackers Broke Into an AI Company's Backroom and Walked Out With Notion's Chats
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: A breach at Fireworks AI, the plumbing behind many AI apps, exposed chat transcripts from Notion AI users. Notion says fewer than 1% of workspaces were touched, and it is telling those users to change any passwords they pasted in.

item.title: Mothman, Sasquatch and a Weeping Squonk Are Getting Their Own Postage Stamps
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service's 2027 lineup includes a Mythical Creatures set of five American cryptids. The least famous of them dissolves into tears when you find it, and the Postal Service calls it "a beloved symbol of anxiety.

item.title: OpenAI Just Fired Its Robot Team — Because the Chatbot Learned to Drive the Robot
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: OpenAI disbanded its stand-alone robotics team after a general model beat the best specialized robot brains 74.8 percent to 51 percent — in simulation. The empty conference booth told the story first.

item.title: Pioner Ran Out of Money Before It Ran Out of Early Access
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The Soviet-flavored survival shooter once pitched as a cousin of Stalker and Tarkov is shutting its servers less than a year after launch. Its studio says it simply cannot pay to keep the lights on.

item.title: The Drunk Raccoon Paid the Rent: $290,000 for the Shelter That Sobered Him Up
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Last year he fell through a liquor store ceiling, drank the inventory, and passed out by the toilet. This week the final tally came in: his face has raised more than fourteen years of donations.

item.title: The Pizza Place Was Dead on Sunday. On Friday, Syracuse Brought It Back.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Twin Trees served its last pizza on Nov. 8 after 69 years. Five days later it reopened — because the customers who packed its final night refused to let the story end there.

item.title: The Supreme Court Will Decide Who Gets to Close the Asylum Door
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The justices agreed Friday to hear the Trump administration's bid to suspend asylum at the southern border. Underneath the immigration fight sits an older question Madison worried over in 1788: where does a president's power stop and Congress's begin?

item.title: The Toddler Dinosaur That Weighed 880 Pounds
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Nyana was about three years old, walked on two legs, and already weighed 400 kilograms. Its kind grew up to rule the Earth as the long-necked giants.

item.title: Typhoid's Deadliest Wound Was a Blood Vessel Problem All Along
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: For more than a century, doctors could describe how typhoid fever tears the small intestine but not why. A Yale lab that has chased one bacterial toxin for 20 years says it finally has the answer.

item.title: The King of AI Is Gone
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Jensen Huang built Nvidia into a $4 trillion company and became the face of the AI boom. In one week, an affair, a spy allegation, and a board meeting ended his 33-year run.

item.title: A Stroke Changed Geralt's Polish Voice. CD Projekt Used AI, With His Blessing, to Turn Back the Clock.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: Jacek Rozenek still records every new line for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion. An AI voice firm then makes him sound like he did a decade ago, so the new scenes don't clash with the old ones.

item.title: Alito Reminds Washington Who Holds the Purse, and Who Holds Only Judgment
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: At the Federalist Society's Scalia dinner, Justice Samuel Alito warned that Congress could "turn off the lights" at the Supreme Court by cutting its money. Hamilton saw that weakness coming in 1788, and the framers built a wall around part of it.

item.title: Euclid Just Mapped 900 Million Galaxies
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: ESA's Euclid telescope released its first big batch of data: more than a billion objects, the foundation of the largest 3D map of the universe ever attempted.

item.title: Mississippi Just Sent Its First Black Senator to Washington Since Reconstruction
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Scott Colom beat a Republican incumbent in the state both parties had written off — on the price of beef, not the culture war.

item.title: Physicists Found a New Knob on the "Magic" Material: Just Stretch It
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: University of Washington researchers squeezed and stretched twisted sheets of carbon one atom thick, and the material's electrical resistance swung more than 100 times harder than an ordinary metal's would.

item.title: Rosalía Wins Album of the Year at the Latin Grammys for a Record Third Time
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The Spanish star took five trophies in Las Vegas for Lux and became the first woman to win the top album prize three times. Argentina's Milo J, 20, beat her for record of the year, and Daddy Yankee brought Diljit Dosanjh on stage.

item.title: Taylor Swift Is Coming Home to the CMAs — First Performance in 13 Years
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Good Morning America announced it on Friday the 13th, which is fitting. Swift takes the CMA stage Nov. 18, with a Single of the Year nomination to go with it.

item.title: The Asteroid That Won't Obey Gravity — and the Lost Soviet Probe It Might Be
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A 36-foot rock called 1998 KY26 is accelerating in a way gravity can't explain. One new study rules out the comet theory. Another team says it might be Phobos 1, lost since 1988.

item.title: Two Horses Walked Onto a Detroit City Bus. Now Every Driver Gets Retrained.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: A viral video shows two saddled horses being led down the aisle of a DDOT bus on 7 Mile and out the back door. The rider says it was a stunt for Black cowboys. The city says horses are not service animals.

item.title: United Airlines to AI Agents: You Can Look, but You Can't Buy
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: United now forbids unauthorized AI assistants from booking, changing or checking in for its flights, even when the customer told them to. Its reasons range from stolen miles to a federal rule that a human has to swear there are no explosives in the bag.

item.title: Wolfenstein 3 Is Real — Xbox's 25th Birthday Brought the News Fans Waited Nine Years For
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: MachineGames is officially making the next Wolfenstein, with BJ Blazkowicz and Grace Walker back. No trailer, no date — just the confirmation.

item.title: The White House Just Told Congress That Investigating It Could Be a Crime
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The counsel's letter to the incoming Oversight chairman reads like a warning shot at Article I itself — and the Democrats answered with two words.
